X.note: The street, walls and light are strong. The figures are the weak point: mannequin-stiff, with blue-trousered and bald, bare-headed figures in mid-stride that look like game assets. The soldiers have no muskets and the red-coat group is a clump. One figure's pose reads as broken. The empty rubble-lined lane in the foreground feels staged.

Y.note: It has the same excellent environment. The figures are more varied (a woman in a white dress, a civilian in a dark coat, soldiers in red with white cross-belts, a blue-coated figure), which tells more of a story. Their poses are still static and they look like standing dolls, some on pegs. The group is better composed, with a clear focal cluster. A long shadow in the middle has no visible source.

why: The environment is identical, but Y's figures are more varied and better grouped and read less like toys, while X's bald blue-trousered walkers look like game assets.
top_fix_for_weaker: Replace the mannequin figures with properly posed, fully dressed soldiers (hats, coats, muskets, varied poses and spacing), and add contact shadows and a slight motion or depth-of-field treatment so they sit in the scene.
anachronisms_seen: bare-headed or bald soldiers in blue trousers with no 1782-style kit (no hats or muskets)
uniform proportions and blank, doll-like faces
pristine, flat-coloured uniforms with no wear in a besieged town
shutters and window frames that look too clean and modern
crisp, bright Union flag at a siege-era flagpole (the 1801 Union design, not the 1782 flag)
